It states that Austin became the capitol in 1888 when the Texas State Capitol was completed. This is incorrect; Austin was designated the permanent capital of Texas in 1845 (upon statehood) and served as the capital from 1845 to 1846 (in the first session) and continuously thereafter, although the seat of government moved temporarily to other locations (like Washington-on-the-Brazos) during the Republic era and Reconstruction. The year 1888 refers to the completion of the current building, not the establishment of the city as the capital. Furthermore, the conclusion that "Omaha has never been the capital of Texas" is correct, but the reasoning provided for the date of Austin's establishment is historically inaccurate, which undermines the reliability of the final answer.
